r1_seen.requests: a stored value-combination (ON-grid, every value in the fit pool)
r1_seen.value_holdout_scope: SCOPE OF THE VALUE HOLD-OUT (⛔ quote no row without this). The hold-out is from the STORE'S FIT POOL, not from the encoder, the decoder or the judge. Those three are frozen, hash-pinned and read-only (charter §A.4) and were fitted on a train split containing EVERY hue and EVERY shape; re-fitting them on a value hold-out would void every wave-2 number and is out of scope. Therefore 'never trained on' means here: THE STORE NEVER HELD A ROW CARRYING THAT VALUE. The decoder can still render the value and the judge can still recognise it — which is what makes rows 2/5/6/7 scorable at all. ⛔ Read end-to-end, 'never seen' is false and the claim dies with it.

knn_proto.note: ⭐ delta_reject is the non-free half of the refusal claim: deleting a value from the store does not move the factor grid, so the §4 no-model rule's delta_reject is exactly 0.0 by construction.

r7_deletion.evidence_note: ⭐ THE strongest instrument. Deleting a value from the store does not move the factor grid, so the no-model rule's delta_reject is exactly 0.0. A changed refusal after a deletion, with NO retraining, is not producible by any syntactic rule.
r7_deletion.requests: post-deletion: rows 3-4 for survivors, row 5 for the deleted value
r7_deletion.value_holdout_scope: SCOPE OF THE VALUE HOLD-OUT (⛔ quote no row without this). The hold-out is from the STORE'S FIT POOL, not from the encoder, the decoder or the judge. Those three are frozen, hash-pinned and read-only (charter §A.4) and were fitted on a train split containing EVERY hue and EVERY shape; re-fitting them on a value hold-out would void every wave-2 number and is out of scope. Therefore 'never trained on' means here: THE STORE NEVER HELD A ROW CARRYING THAT VALUE. The decoder can still render the value and the judge can still recognise it — which is what makes rows 2/5/6/7 scorable at all. ⛔ Read end-to-end, 'never seen' is false and the claim dies with it.
